clues: Of Zeke and whoever came at 10 a.m., one had ordered the rye loaf and the other the cinnamon bun.
One of the 7 a.m. and 10 a.m. customers took the rye loaf, and the other took the layer cake.
Lou came in before whoever ordered the baguettes.
Zeke came in after the baguettes had been collected.
hints: Look at the baguettes column in the box where customers meet orders. Who could possibly have ordered them?
Every comparison hides an X. Clues 3 and 4 compare Lou and Zeke with the baguettes' customer. Could either of them be that customer?
So Milo ordered the baguettes. By clues 3 and 4, Lou came before Milo and Zeke after him, and clue 1 keeps Zeke off 10 a.m.

solution.key_idea: Clues 3, 4 and 5 each rule out one customer for the baguettes, so they were Milo's, and he came between Lou and Zeke.
steps: Clue 3 rules out Lou for the baguettes, clue 4 rules out Zeke, and clue 5 rules out Nico. So Milo ordered the baguettes.
By clues 3 and 4, Lou came in before Milo, and Milo before Zeke.
Clue 1 keeps Zeke off 10 a.m., so Zeke came at 9 a.m., Milo at 8 a.m. and Lou at 7 a.m. Nico came at 10 a.m.
By clue 1, Zeke and Nico had the rye loaf and the cinnamon bun between them, so Lou had the layer cake.
Lou had the layer cake at 7 a.m., so by clue 2 the 10 a.m. customer, Nico, took the rye loaf. Zeke took the cinnamon bun.
solution.epilogue: Rosa's book read Lou, Milo, Zeke and Nico, from 7 to 10 a.m. Zeke carried the plate-sized cinnamon bun out with both hands, and Nico swore it was bigger than his boat.

tip: Every comparison hides an X: nobody comes in earlier than themselves.
